Subject: POC initialization playbook — proposal & timeline

Hi Lena,

Thanks for the kickoff yesterday. Attached is a short draft of the mutual action plan (MAP_v0.3.pdf) focused on the engineering milestones for the POC environment: org setup, API key provisioning, IP allowlist, and optional VPC peering. High-level asks:

- Confirm the org admin contact and preferred org ID for onboarding.
- Share a primary and secondary CIDR (or confirm permission to propose test CIDR).
- Procurement contact so we can provide the commercial artifacts.

Proposed runway: 3 weeks from org activation to a staged evaluation (week 1: org & keys; week 2: networking & sample traffic; week 3: smoke tests and handoff). If that works I can circulate a schedule with owner names.

I’ve cc’d Laura (eng enablement) to track activation, and Ben for the peering template. Attachments: MAP_v0.3.pdf (draft).

Thanks,
Rishi

Lena — quick technical callouts on peering and the suggested test CIDR:

- 10.55.128.0/24 looks safe given the ranges you described. It’s routable and small enough to limit exposure.
- Peering mode: cross-account VPC peering (direct) will be the fastest to set up for a single POC environment. If you need TGW we can adapt but it adds 24–48 hours with infra approvals.
- Routing: after peering, add the route to your route table pointing 10.55.128.0/24 -> peering attachment. We recommend no-propagation on subnets that host sensitive services.
- NAT: if you require outbound NAT from Redwood side, we can provision an egress gateway; otherwise we’ll use ephemeral source NAT from our POC subnet.

Sample snippet included in vpc-peering-request.yaml. Happy to jump on a quick 30-min call if this helps.

Ben
